subject: Anthropology
title: Residence Rules
description: A quick win: understand Residence Rules.

hook.text: Where do newlyweds live? With his parents, her parents, or on their own? The answer shapes power and daily life.

buildup.text: Residence rules determine where a couple lives after marriage: patrilocal, matrilocal, neolocal, or other arrangements.

discovery.text: Patrilocal residence is most common. The wife moves to the husband's family. Matrilocal is the reverse pattern.

twist.text: Where you live decides who you depend on. Patrilocal wives are isolated from their kin; matrilocal husbands are.

climax.text: Residence rules shape daily power. Living near your own kin gives you allies, support, and bargaining strength.

punchline.text: Where you live after marriage decides who has power.

quiz.question: What is patrilocal residence?
options: The couple lives with the wife's family
The couple lives with the husband's family
The couple moves to a new place alone

details.summary: Residence rules determine where a newly married couple lives. Patrilocal residence means living with the husband's family, matrilocal with the wife's family, and neolocal means establishing an independent household. Each pattern shapes family dynamics and power.
details.whyItMatters: Where couples live after marriage determines who controls resources, who provides childcare, and whose kin group gains a new member. Residence rules are a powerful force shaping gender dynamics and family structure.
takeaways: Patrilocal residence places couples with the husband's family
Matrilocal residence places couples with the wife's family
Neolocal residence establishes independent new households

faq.question: Which residence pattern is most common globally?
faq.answer: Patrilocal residence is most common cross-culturally, found in roughly 70 percent of documented societies. This pattern correlates with patrilineal descent and contributes to male control over property and political authority in many cultures.

faq.question: How does residence pattern affect gender dynamics?
faq.answer: In patrilocal systems, women leave their support network and enter their husband's family as relative strangers. In matrilocal systems, women remain near their mothers and sisters, often resulting in greater female autonomy and mutual support.
